subtype: Approach: gives a task a fixed time slot [Action]
passage:
The house was full of relatives for the wedding, and someone was tuning a dholak downstairs. Abhinav had maths homework and wanted to go out to play later. His sister Nandini handed him the kitchen timer.

"Twenty minutes," he said, turning the dial, and he sat in a corner of the balcony with his notebook. He did the first six sums, put a star beside a hard one, and the timer rang while he was halfway through the seventh. He stopped, even though he wanted to finish. He drank water, stretched, and looked at the street for five minutes. Then he opened his science book and set the timer again.

qa.q: What did Nandini hand to Abhinav?
qa.a: Nandini handed him the kitchen timer.

qa.q: What did Abhinav feel when the timer rang halfway through the seventh sum?
qa.a: Abhinav was probably torn, since he wanted to finish the seventh sum but stopped anyway when the timer rang.

qa.q: What could Abhinav do about the hard sum he starred?
qa.a: Abhinav could ask Nandini or the teacher about it, or try it again after the break, so it does not eat up the rest of his time.

qa.q: How might Nandini see Abhinav's plan in such a noisy house?
qa.a: Nandini might be glad the timer helped him stay focused despite the noise, and relieved he was doing the homework instead of skipping it.

grounding: Shows a boy giving maths homework a fixed twenty-minute slot, stopping at the ring and taking a short break.

subtype: Approach: gives a task a fixed time slot [Action]
passage:
Jatin's maths homework always took the whole evening. He would do a sum, look out of the window of their Indore flat, sharpen a pencil, do half a sum.
On Monday his elder sister Usha put her old kitchen timer on his desk. "Twenty minutes. Only maths. When it rings, stop."
Jatin twisted the dial to twenty. He started. At minute twelve he wanted to check the cricket score, but the timer was ticking, so he did the next sum instead.
Ring! He had finished eight sums. He put down his pencil, went to the kitchen, drank water and ate two biscuits. Five minutes.
Then he set the timer again, this time for Hindi.
By seven he was done with everything. "That's the earliest ever," Usha said.

qa.q: How many sums had Jatin finished when the timer rang?
How might Jatin have felt at minute twelve when he wanted to check the score?
qa.a: He was probably tempted and restless, but the ticking timer helped him stay with the next sum.

qa.q: What else could Jatin try if twenty minutes feels too long some days?
qa.a: He could try fifteen-minute slots with short breaks, since the goal is steady focus, not a fixed number.

qa.q: How does Usha see Jatin's evening?
qa.a: Usha is pleased and a little proud, since her timer helped him finish earlier than ever.

grounding: It shows a boy giving maths homework a fixed twenty-minute slot, stopping when the timer rings and taking a short break before the next subject.

passage:
"Timer's on," Dhruv said, putting the phone face down on the study table. "Twenty minutes for maths."
His cousin Pallavi looked up from her drawing. "And then?"
"Then I stop. Even if I'm not done."
"Why would you stop if you're not done?"
"Because otherwise I do maths for two hours and never get to science. Miss told us to try it."
Pallavi went back to her drawing. The room was quiet except for Dhruv's pencil.
The alarm buzzed. Dhruv groaned. "Two sums left."
"So finish them!"
"No. Break." He stretched, went to the balcony for five minutes, came back and set the timer for science. "The two sums get their own slot after dinner."
Pallavi shook her head. "You're so strange."
"I'm finishing my homework on time for once," Dhruv grinned.

qa.q: How long did Dhruv spend on the balcony?
qa.a: He went to the balcony for five minutes.

qa.q: How did Dhruv feel when the alarm buzzed with two sums left?
qa.a: He felt a bit annoyed, which is why he groaned, but he stuck to his plan and took the break.

qa.q: What else could Dhruv try for the two unfinished sums?
qa.a: He could give them a short fixed slot after dinner, as he planned, so they don't grow into a whole evening.

qa.q: How does Pallavi see Dhruv's timer plan?
qa.a: Pallavi finds it strange to stop before finishing, but can see he is getting his homework done on time.

grounding: It shows a boy setting a timer for twenty minutes of maths homework, stopping when it rings and taking a short break before the next subject.
